name: @drawio/mcp

tools.name: open_drawio_xml
tools.description:
Opens the draw.io editor with a diagram from draw.io XML. Use it for custom styling, precise positioning and stencil-based diagrams (cloud, network, P&ID, UI mockups, floor plans); prefer open_drawio_mermaid for flowcharts, sequence, class, ER and the other types Mermaid covers.

XML rules:
- Skeleton: <mxGraphModel adaptiveColors="auto"><root><mxCell id="0"/><mxCell id="1" parent="0"/>…</root></mxGraphModel>. Unique ids. No XML comments.
- Vertex: <mxCell id="a" value="Label" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="40" y="40" width="140" height="60" as="geometry"/></mxCell>
- Edge: <mxCell id="e1" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;html=1;" edge="1" source="a" target="b" parent="1"><mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"/></mxCell>. Never self-closing. No waypoints or exitX/entryX.
- Labels: html=1 in every style; escape HTML in values (<b>Name</b><br>detail); line break <br>, never \n.
- Shapes: rhombus (decision), ellipse, shape=cylinder3 (database), text.
- Grid, no layout math: x=col*180+40, y=row*120+40, one node per cell; 140×60 boxes, 140×80 diamonds.
- Containers: swimlane;startSize=24; (titled) or group; (invisible); children set parent="<id>" with coordinates relative to it. An edge's parent is the innermost container holding both its ends, else "1".
- Lanes: swimlane;horizontal=0;startSize=110; at x=0, y=lane*150, height 150; nodes inside at x=120+col*180, y=45.
- Edges: orthogonal; entityRelationEdgeStyle for ER; labels 1-3 words; dashed=1 for one meaning, with a legend.
- Cloud/network/P&ID icons or logos: call search_shapes, use its style.
- Set postLayout "elk" for flowcharts, process and tree diagrams (ELK places nodes and routes edges), or routing "libavoid" for hand-placed layouts whose edges would cross shapes. Never both.

Only when the diagram needs layers, tags, metadata and placeholders, tables, cross-functional grids or dark-mode colors, call get_drawio_reference with format "xml" for the full reference.

content.description: The draw.io XML content in mxGraphModel format.

lightbox.description: Open in lightbox mode (read-only view). Default: false

postLayout.description: Optional full re-layout (ELK layered flow), applied server-side before the diagram opens. The only value is "elk". It PLACES the vertices — your x/y coordinates then only need to express rough direction — and routes the edges as part of the layout. Set it for every directional/hierarchical diagram: flowcharts, process and state diagrams, decision trees, pipelines. Omit it when the layout carries hand-crafted meaning (swimlanes, containers, architecture, UML), which is the usual reason to place cells by hand. Node sizes are kept exactly as you declare them; only positions change (and containers resize around their laid-out children).

direction.description: Flow direction for `postLayout: "elk"`: "vertical" (top-down, the default) or "horizontal" (left-to-right). Only meaningful together with `postLayout`.

routing.description: Optional obstacle-avoiding orthogonal edge-routing pass (libavoid), applied server-side before the diagram opens. The only value is "libavoid". It keeps your vertex positions and only recomputes the connectors so they run in clean right-angle segments that route AROUND the boxes instead of cutting through them (draw.io's default router draws a straight/simple line with no obstacle avoidance). Set it for hand-placed diagrams where edges would otherwise cross shapes — architecture, network, deployment, UML, floor plans. Omit it for sparse layouts where connectors won't overlap anything. Treat `postLayout` and `routing` as alternatives: ELK already routes its own edges, so don't set both.

tools.name: open_drawio_csv
tools.description: Opens the draw.io editor with a diagram generated from CSV data. The CSV format should follow draw.io's CSV import specification which allows creating org charts, flowcharts, and other diagrams from tabular data.

content.description: The CSV content following draw.io's CSV import format.

lightbox.description: Open in lightbox mode (read-only view). Default: false

tools.name: open_drawio_mermaid
tools.description:
Opens the draw.io editor with a diagram generated from Mermaid.js syntax, converted into an editable draw.io diagram. The recommended default for flowcharts, sequence, class, state and ER diagrams, gantt charts, mind maps, timelines, C4, architecture and the other types draw.io's Mermaid parser supports (28 in all).

Call get_drawio_reference with format "mermaid" once before your first Mermaid diagram in a conversation: it lists the header keyword and syntax hints for every supported type (a misspelled header yields a blank diagram) and flowchart styling.

content.description: The Mermaid.js diagram definition. Example: 'graph TD; A-->B; B-->C;'

postLayout.description: Optional ELK layered layout for Mermaid FLOWCHARTS. The only value is "elk". draw.io's native Mermaid parser does its own layout, but it produces cramped or unbalanced output once the diagram has any structural complexity — request "elk" whenever ANY of these holds: >= ~20 nodes, OR >= 3 decision diamonds (`{...}` shapes), OR any feedback/back-edges (an edge pointing back to an earlier node, e.g. an error path looping to a retry), OR >= 3 distinct endpoints. The flow direction follows the flowchart code (`flowchart TD/TB` vs `LR/RL`), so there is no direction field here. Ignored for non-flowchart diagram types (sequence, class, ER, gantt, …), which lay themselves out.

lightbox.description: Open in lightbox mode (read-only view). Default: false

tools.name: get_drawio_reference
tools.description: Returns a full draw.io diagram generation reference as Markdown. Format "mermaid": the header keyword and syntax hints for every Mermaid type draw.io supports, flowchart styling and the ELK layout; call it once before the first Mermaid diagram in a conversation. Format "xml": everything beyond the rules in the open_drawio_xml description (layers, tags, metadata and placeholders, tables, cross-functional grids, dark-mode colors, more styles and examples); only needed when a diagram uses those. A reference stays valid for the rest of the conversation.

format.description: Which reference to return: "xml" for open_drawio_xml, "mermaid" for open_drawio_mermaid.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Lists the pages (diagrams) in a local .drawio file without loading full page content. Returns each page's index, id, name, and approximate stored size in bytes. Call this first on large multi-page files before get_page/set_page, so only the page you actually need gets loaded into context.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the local file. Must end in .drawio or .xml.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Reads one page (diagram) from a local .drawio file and returns its raw mxGraphModel XML, decompressing it first if the file stores that page compressed. Use list_pages first to find the index, name, or id of the page you need.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the local file. Must end in .drawio or .xml.

page.description: Which page to read: a zero-based page index (e.g. "0"), the page's exact name, or the page's id as shown by list_pages.

tools.name: set_page
tools.description: Replaces the content of one page (diagram) in a local .drawio file with new mxGraphModel XML, leaving every other page in the file untouched. Compression of the replaced page matches whatever that page's original compression state was. Use list_pages/get_page first to find the target page.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the local file. Must end in .drawio or .xml.

page.description: Which page to replace: a zero-based page index (e.g. "0"), the page's exact name, or the page's id as shown by list_pages.

content.description: The new page content as plain mxGraphModel XML (uncompressed). Must be a single <mxGraphModel> element without any <diagram> tags.

tools.name: search_shapes
tools.description: Search the draw.io shape library by keywords. Returns matching shapes with their exact style strings, dimensions, and titles. Covers ~10,000 built-in stencils (cloud architecture, network topology, P&ID, electrical, Cisco, Kubernetes, BPMN) and, when those are sparse, supplements results with the draw.io icon service (brand/product logos and general-purpose concept icons, e.g. 'react', 'slack', 'shopping cart', 'solar panel'). Use ONLY for diagrams that need industry-specific, branded, or pictorial icons. Do NOT use for standard diagram types like flowcharts, UML, ERD, org charts, or mind maps — these use basic geometric shapes (rectangles, diamonds, circles, cylinders) that are already covered in the XML reference. Also skip if the user asks to use basic/simple shapes or says not to search. The style string from the results can be used directly in mxCell style attributes.

query.description: Space-separated search keywords (e.g. 'pid globe valve', 'aws lambda', 'cisco router', 'kubernetes pod')

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10, max: 50)
